-- Ground truth is used ONLY by scripts/evaluate_reconciliation.py (offline
-- evaluation) - never joined into the marts a real claims team would query,
-- since a real platform doesn't have access to its own ground truth.
select
    claim_id,
    policyholder,
    policy_number,
    cast(claim_date as date) as claim_date,
    category,
    item_description,
    cast(item_value as double) as item_value,
    true_severity,
    cast(claimed_amount as double) as claimed_amount,
    incident_description,
    cast(is_injected_mismatch as boolean) as is_injected_mismatch
from "warehouse"."raw"."claims_ground_truth"

-- MetricFlow (dbt's Semantic Layer engine) requires a "time spine" model
-- in the project even though none of this platform's metrics use a time
-- dimension - claims aren't currently modeled with a date grain. A plain
-- DuckDB generate_series stands in for what dbt_utils.date_spine would
-- otherwise build, without adding a package dependency for one table.
select cast(date_day as date) as date_day
from generate_series(cast('2020-01-01' as date), cast('2030-12-31' as date), interval 1 day) as t(date_day)

select
    claim_id,
    policyholder,
    policy_number,
    claim_date,
    category,
    item_description,
    try_cast(item_value as double) as item_value,
    try_cast(claimed_amount as double) as claimed_amount
from "warehouse"."raw"."extraction_regex"

-- LLM-extracted fields, cast defensively: document_ai/llm_field_extraction.py
-- found the model sometimes returns item_value/claimed_amount as a
-- dollar-formatted string ("$214.20") rather than a bare number despite
-- being instructed otherwise - try_cast handles that instead of failing
-- the whole row, and a genuinely unparseable value becomes NULL (visible
-- in the marts' extraction_quality flag) rather than crashing the build.
select
    claim_id,
    coalesce(extraction_failed, true) as extraction_failed,
    policyholder,
    policy_number,
    claim_date,
    category,
    item_description,
    try_cast(regexp_replace(cast(item_value as varchar), '[$,]', '', 'g') as double) as item_value,
    try_cast(regexp_replace(cast(claimed_amount as varchar), '[$,]', '', 'g') as double) as claimed_amount
from "warehouse"."raw"."extraction_llm"

select
    claim_id,
    claimed_fraction,
    explanation as flag_explanation
from "warehouse"."raw"."reconciliation_flags"

select

-- One row per claim, combining both document-extraction pipelines with a
-- regex fallback (used only when the LLM extraction guardrail rejected
-- the response - see document_ai/llm_field_extraction.py), the CV
-- severity prediction, and any reconciliation flag. This is the single
-- place the "which extraction source won" decision is made, so it's
-- auditable in one spot rather than scattered across the marts layer.

with extraction as (
    select
        coalesce(llm.claim_id, rx.claim_id) as claim_id,
        case when llm.extraction_failed then 'regex_fallback' else 'llm' end as extraction_source,
        coalesce(nullif(llm.extraction_failed, false) is null and not llm.extraction_failed, false) as llm_succeeded,
        coalesce(llm.policyholder, rx.policyholder) as policyholder,
        coalesce(llm.policy_number, rx.policy_number) as policy_number,
        coalesce(try_cast(llm.claim_date as date), try_cast(rx.claim_date as date)) as claim_date,
        coalesce(llm.category, rx.category) as category,
        coalesce(llm.item_description, rx.item_description) as item_description,
        coalesce(
            case when llm.extraction_failed then null else llm.item_value end,
            rx.item_value
        ) as item_value,
        coalesce(
            case when llm.extraction_failed then null else llm.claimed_amount end,
            rx.claimed_amount
        ) as claimed_amount
    from "warehouse"."main"."stg_extraction_llm" llm
    full outer join "warehouse"."main"."stg_extraction_regex" rx using (claim_id)
)

select
    e.claim_id,
    e.extraction_source,
    e.policyholder,
    e.policy_number,
    e.claim_date,
    e.category,
    e.item_description,
    e.item_value,
    e.claimed_amount,
    v.predicted_severity,
    v.confidence as vision_confidence,
    (f.claim_id is not null) as is_flagged,
    f.claimed_fraction as flagged_claimed_fraction,
    f.flag_explanation
from extraction e
left join "warehouse"."main"."stg_vision_predictions" v using (claim_id)
left join "warehouse"."main"."stg_reconciliation_flags" f using (claim_id)

-- The governed, contract-enforced fact table - the ONE place claims ops,
-- finance, and the dashboard are meant to query. Enforcing a contract here
-- (see _marts.yml) means a future change to an upstream extraction
-- pipeline that silently changes a column's type breaks the dbt build
-- loudly, at build time, instead of breaking a downstream dashboard query
-- silently, at 2am.

select
    claim_id,
    extraction_source,
    policyholder,
    policy_number,
    claim_date,
    category,
    item_description,
    item_value,
    claimed_amount,
    round(claimed_amount / nullif(item_value, 0), 4) as claimed_fraction_of_value,
    predicted_severity,
    vision_confidence,
    is_flagged,
    flag_explanation
from "warehouse"."main"."int_claims_reconciled"

with all_values as (

    select
        predicted_severity as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from "warehouse"."main"."fct_claims"
    group by predicted_severity

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'none','minor','moderate','severe'
)

with all_values as (

    select
        extraction_source as value_field,
        count(*) as n_records

    from "warehouse"."main"."fct_claims"
    group by extraction_source

)

select *
from all_values
where value_field not in (
    'llm','regex_fallback'
)
